learn.hook: Your body is like a busy factory. Food brings in the workers that keep it running!
points: Nutrients are the useful parts of food that help our body work, grow and stay healthy.
Carbohydrates give us energy. Rice, wheat, potatoes and bajra are rich in carbohydrates.
Proteins help our body grow and repair itself. Dal, rajma, milk, paneer, eggs and fish are rich in proteins.
Fats also give energy. Ghee, butter, oil and nuts have fats. We need them only in small amounts.
Vitamins and minerals protect us from illness. Fruits and vegetables are full of them. Milk gives calcium for strong bones and teeth.

example.q: Think it through: Raju plays football for two hours and feels tired. Which food will give him energy quickly: a banana or a glass of water?
steps: Water is very important, but it gives no energy.
example.answer: The banana, because it has carbohydrates that give energy.

learn.reallife: Look at your lunch box. Can you find one energy food, one body-building food and one protective food?

games.title: Which nutrient is it rich in?
Nutrient and its job
pairs: Help us grow and repair the body
Give energy, needed in small amounts

quiz.q: Which nutrient mainly gives us energy?
quiz.explain: Carbohydrates in foods like rice, roti and potatoes give us energy to work and play.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the jobs of different nutrients

quiz.q: Which food is rich in protein?
quiz.explain: Dals like moong are rich in proteins, which help the body grow.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which foods are body-building foods

quiz.q: Why do we need vitamins and minerals?
quiz.explain: Vitamins and minerals keep our body working well and help protect us from falling ill.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that vitamins and minerals are protective

quiz.q: Which of these is rich in fat?
quiz.explain: Ghee is almost all fat. We need fats only in small amounts.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise foods that have fats

quiz.q: Milk is good for strong bones and teeth because it has…
quiz.explain: Milk, curd and paneer have calcium, a mineral that builds strong bones and teeth.
quiz.mistake: Does not link milk with calcium

quiz.q: Amla and oranges are rich in which vitamin?
quiz.explain: Amla, oranges and lemons are rich in vitamin C, which helps fight illness.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the vitamins found in citrus fruits

quiz.q: Our body can make vitamin D when our skin gets…
quiz.explain: When sunlight falls on our skin, the body makes vitamin D. It also helps bones stay strong.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the sunlight-vitamin D link

quiz.q: Which group of foods helps our body grow?
quiz.explain: Eggs, fish, paneer and dal are rich in proteins, the body-building nutrient.
quiz.mistake: Thinks tasty snacks help the body grow

teach.ask: Gappu only wants to eat sweets. Can you tell him about the nutrients in food and what they do?
teach.praise: Yum! Carbohydrates give energy, proteins help us grow and vitamins and minerals protect us. Gappu will eat dal and fruits too!
teach.nudge: Which nutrient gives energy, and which one helps us grow?

learn.hook: A good plate is like a good team: everyone plays a part!
points: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals.
We also need roughage (fibre) and water. Roughage from fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps us digest food.
A thali with roti or rice, dal, a green vegetable, curd and salad is a balanced meal.
Too much fried food, sweets, chips and fizzy drinks is not good for health.
Wash hands before eating, eat slowly, chew well and do not waste food.

example.q: Think it through: Tanya's lunch is a plate of rice and potato curry. What should she add to make it more balanced?
steps: Rice and potato both give mostly carbohydrates.
She needs proteins, so she can add dal or curd.
She needs vitamins, minerals and roughage, so she can add a green vegetable or salad.
example.answer: Add dal or curd and a green vegetable or salad.

learn.reallife: Help plan one day's meals at home. Try to fit all the food groups in!

games.title: Healthy eating: true or false?
items: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts.
Balance means we get some of each nutrient our body needs.
Roughage, or fibre, helps food move through our body.
Eating only sweets is a balanced diet.
Sweets give mostly sugar. We also need proteins, vitamins and minerals.
We should wash our hands before eating.
Washing hands removes germs before they reach our food.
Drinking water is important for good health.
Our body needs water to work properly.

quiz.q: What is a balanced diet?
options: Food with all the nutrients in the right amounts
Food eaten while standing on one leg
quiz.explain: A balanced diet gives the body all the nutrients it needs in the right amounts.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one kind of food is enough

quiz.q: Which meal is the most balanced?
options: Roti, dal, green vegetable, curd and salad
quiz.explain: This thali has carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, minerals and roughage.
quiz.mistake: Picks the tastiest meal instead of the balanced one

quiz.q: What does roughage do for us?
options: It makes us taller in one day
quiz.explain: Roughage, or fibre, helps food move through the body and keeps the stomach healthy.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the job of roughage

quiz.q: Which of these is rich in roughage?
quiz.explain: Fruits like guava, especially with their skin, are rich in fibre.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which foods have fibre

quiz.q: Why should we not eat too much fried food and sweets?
options: They are bad for health if eaten too much
quiz.explain: Too much oil and sugar can harm our teeth, heart and weight.
quiz.mistake: Thinks snacks can replace proper meals

quiz.q: Arun's dinner is roti and dal. Which item adds vitamins and roughage?
quiz.explain: Vegetables add vitamins, minerals and roughage to the meal.
quiz.mistake: Adds more of the same nutrient instead of a missing one

quiz.q: Which is a good eating habit?
options: Eating in a hurry without chewing
Chewing food well and eating slowly
quiz.explain: Chewing well helps digestion, and eating slowly helps us enjoy food.
quiz.mistake: Does not know good eating habits

quiz.q: Besides food, what else must we drink plenty of every day?
quiz.explain: Clean water keeps our body working well, especially on hot days.
quiz.mistake: Thinks sugary drinks can replace water

teach.ask: Gappu filled his plate with only laddoos. What is a balanced diet, Gappu wonders?
teach.praise: Perfect! A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts. Gappu will add dal and vegetables to his plate.
teach.nudge: Can one kind of food give Gappu all the nutrients he needs?

learn.hook: Idli in Chennai, dhokla in Ahmedabad, litti chokha in Patna: India is a giant tasty menu!
points: Food in each region depends on the crops that grow there and the weather.
Rice grows well where there is a lot of rain, so it is a main food in many coastal and eastern states like Kerala, West Bengal, Odisha and Assam.
Wheat is a main food in Punjab and Haryana. Bajra grows in dry Rajasthan, and ragi is popular in Karnataka.
People living near the sea or rivers often eat fish, like machher jhol in West Bengal and fish curry in Goa and Kerala.
Millets like bajra, jowar and ragi need less water and are very healthy. The year 2023 was the International Year of Millets.

example.q: Think it through: Why is coconut used so much in Kerala food?
steps: Kerala is on the coast and gets heavy rain.
Coconut trees grow very well in warm, wet coastal places.
People cook with what grows near them.
example.answer: Because coconut trees grow well in Kerala's warm, rainy coastal weather.

learn.reallife: Ask your grandparents what they ate as children. Is it the same as the food of your region today?

games.title: Match the dish to the state
pairs: Makki di roti and sarson da saag

items.q: Main grain of rainy, coastal states
Millet that grows in dry Rajasthan
Tree whose fruit flavours Kerala food

quiz.q: Dhokla is a well-known dish from which state?
quiz.explain: Dhokla is a soft, steamed snack from Gujarat.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up dishes and their states

quiz.q: Why is rice a main food in states like Kerala and West Bengal?
options: Because rice grows well where there is a lot of rain
Because wheat is not allowed there
quiz.explain: Rice fields need a lot of water, and these states get heavy rain.
quiz.mistake: Does not link crops with rainfall

quiz.q: Bajra is grown in Rajasthan because…
options: it grows only under the sea
it needs a lot of rain
quiz.explain: Bajra is a millet that grows well in hot, dry places with little rain.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all crops need a lot of water

quiz.q: Which dish is from Bihar?
quiz.explain: Litti chokha, baked wheat balls with mashed vegetables, is a famous dish of Bihar.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up regional dishes

quiz.q: The International Year of Millets was celebrated in which year?
quiz.explain: The United Nations named 2023 the International Year of Millets. India suggested the idea.
quiz.mistake: Does not remember the year of millets

quiz.q: People living near the sea in Goa often eat…
quiz.explain: Fish is easy to get near the sea, so fish curry with rice is popular in Goa.
quiz.mistake: Does not link coastal areas with fish

quiz.q: Which of these is a millet?
quiz.explain: Ragi, bajra and jowar are millets. Rice and wheat are other grains.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every grain is a millet

quiz.q: Makki di roti and sarson da saag are a famous winter meal of…
quiz.explain: This meal of maize roti and mustard greens is loved in Punjab.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up regional dishes

teach.ask: Gappu flew from Kerala to Rajasthan, and the food was so different! Why do regions eat different food?
teach.praise: Delicious! People eat what grows well in their region, and that depends on rain and weather.
teach.nudge: Does rice grow better in a rainy place or a dry place?
